title: Salted shingle hashing and staggered TTL strategy to reduce embedding lookup latency and duplicate work
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The reranking/embedding endpoint sees high variability in embedding lookup latency and significant duplicate compute for short prefixes and near-duplicate content. Existing prefix caches use coarse canonicalization which results in redundant embedding requests across tenants and small edits. We need a cache strategy that reduces tail latency, minimizes duplicate inference work, and preserves freshness for tenant-scoped or frequently-updated content.

Proposal: Implement a salted shingle content-hash as the canonical cache key and a staggered TTL tiering policy. Key components: 1) Shingle-based fingerprinting: split input into overlapping n-grams (shingles) and hash the shingle set to produce a compact content fingerprint robust to small edits. 2) Tenant-aware salt: incorporate a tenant salt (rotatable) into the hash to avoid cross-tenant collisions while still enabling cross-tenant dedupe for public data when configured. 3) Tiered storage: an in-process hot LRU (small, single-node) for prefix-heavy hotkeys with very short TTLs (100-500ms) and a distributed replicated cache (global) with longer TTLs (10s-5m) for warm hits. 4) Staggered TTL policy: assign TTLs probabilistically based on observed update frequency and semantic-change score (derived from shingle divergence) to avoid thundering herd and to prefer freshness for volatile content. 5) Prefetch hooks: when a request misses, trigger opportunistic prefetch for likely-followup prefixes in the request stream (based on per-tenant prefix transition model). 6) Graceful staleness: return slightly-stale embed + kv-fallback to live compute for high-importance requests and expose a staleness flag in response metadata for downstream rerankers.

Goals: reduce median embedding lookup latency by ~20% and 95th percentile by at least 25% under typical reranking workloads; reduce duplicate embedding compute (measured by redundant model calls per minute) by >=30% for prefix-heavy traffic without regressing rerank quality.

Implementation notes: design includes a new cache key format v2: {algo:v2, tenant_salt_id, shingle_hash, prefix_len_bucket}. Salt rotation will be recorded in tenant metadata and older salts remain valid for a grace period to avoid invalidating live caches during rotation. We will add metrics: cache_hit_rate_v2, shingle_divergence_hist, tenant_salt_evictions, prefetch_success_rate, staleness_frac.

Compatibility and rollouts: initial rollout as an opt-in routing rule: 10% of traffic to canary pool with same model/replicas. Canary will run both v1 and v2 cache lookups (shadow) for comparison, but only v2 will be used to serve on successful rollout. Fallback to v1 on regression.

Risk considerations: salted keys increase operational complexity (salt management) and older caches must be invalidated carefully. Shingle hashing adds CPU cost at the API layer; mitigate with SIMD-optimized implementation and sampling. Prefetching may increase load; use budgeted background workers and rate-limit per-tenant.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Diego A.: Implemented prototype for shingle hashing using 5-grams; microbenchmarks show 2.4us per hash for 512-char inputs (Go SIMD).

2026-03-03 - Priya Rao (review): Liked tenant salt approach; requested clarifications on key rotation semantics and whether salts are tenant-managed vs platform-managed. Asked to add KMS interaction only if salts become secrets.
2026-03-04 - Maya C.: Updated design to keep salts non-secret (opaque tenant IDs) unless customer requests per-tenant secret salts; added salt rotation window of 48 hours and auto-replay grace.

2026-03-05 - QA: End-to-end test plan added. Will validate: correctness on small edits (insert/delete), dedupe rate under synthetic duplicate workload, and staleness signal propagation to reranker. Added test harness to replay production prefix streams at 2x.

2026-03-06 - Perf: Shadow canary run on 5% traffic. Observed preliminary results: shadow hit-rate_v2=44% vs v1=31% on sample tenant set; median lookup latency down 18% in canary path; 95th reduced 21%. Prefetch success small initially (6%) — need better prefix transition model.
2026-03-07 - Security: Confirmed no changes to KMS required for default non-secret salts. If tenant opts for secret salt, schedule security review.
2026-03-08 - Diego A.: Implemented staggered TTL sampler and prefetched top-3 prefixes per session. Preparing canary pipeline config for 10% rollout and monitoring dashboards.
